kjv: on earth peace, good will toward men
mine: on earth peace among those with whom he (God) is pleased
note: TR has nominative "eudokia" (a third clause, "good will toward men"); Sinaiticus (first hand), Vaticanus, A, D have genitive "eudokias" ("people of [God's] good pleasure"), a Semitic idiom also found at Qumran; one letter changes the angels' message.

kjv: And Joseph and his (Jesus') mother marvelled
mine: And his (Jesus') father and his mother marveled
note: TR "Ioseph" replaces "ho pater autou" of Sinaiticus, Vaticanus, D, W, evidently to avoid calling Joseph Jesus' father; Luke himself uses "his parents" (2:41) and Mary says "your father and I" (2:48).

kjv: Joseph and his (Jesus') mother knew not of it
mine: His (Jesus') parents did not know it
note: TR "Ioseph kai he meter autou" against "hoi goneis autou" in Sinaiticus, Vaticanus, D, for the same reason as 2:33.

mine: the time came for their purification
note: TR "autes" ("her") against "auton" ("their") in Sinaiticus, Vaticanus, A, L.

kjv: wist ye not that I (Jesus) must be about my Father's business?
mine: Did you not know that I (Jesus) must be in my Father's house?
note: en tois tou patros mou ("in the things of my Father") most naturally means "in my Father's house" (contrasted with searching elsewhere); "business" is a possible but less likely sense.

kjv: there was no room for them (Joseph and Mary) in the inn
mine: there was no place for them (Joseph and Mary) in the guest room
note: katalyma is a guest room or lodging (the same word for the "guest chamber" of 22:11), not necessarily a commercial inn (pandocheion, 10:34).
